edges.description: Chronic active gastritis is the first stage of the multistep sequence that constitutes the carcinogenic substrate node.

Dysplastic epithelium breaches the basement membrane and becomes invasive carcinoma. The intervening step is the transition from high-grade dysplasia to invasion, which is not a separate node in this entry.

Invasive carcinoma penetrates the gastric serosa and sheds cells into the peritoneal cavity. Serosal penetration and transcoelomic shedding are the known intervening steps and are not separate nodes in this entry. This is the weaker of the two routes into peritoneal disease: peritoneal spread is the diffuse-type pattern, and intestinal-type tumours preferentially recur in the liver by haematogenous spread, which this entry does not currently model as its own node. The edge asserts that intestinal-type disease also reaches the peritoneum, not that this is where it predominates.
Without E-cadherin the epithelial sheet loses junctional cohesion and cells detach and infiltrate individually.

Non-cohesive cells permeate the gastric wall and, on reaching the serosa, seed the peritoneal cavity - the characteristic route of spread for diffuse-type disease. Transmural infiltration and serosal penetration are the known intervening steps.

Implants seeded on the peritoneum and omentum depend on the surrounding stromal compartment for the angiogenic support that lets a deposit grow beyond a micrometastasis. Adipocyte-derived CXCL2 and tumour VEGFA induction are the known intervening steps.

The organism colonises the gastric mucosa and the chronic active gastritis at this node is its direct consequence, the first step of the carcinogenic cascade that produces the primary tumour. Nothing intervenes between the infection and the gastritis it causes.

A review-level risk-factor listing names smoking alongside H. pylori and salt intake, but does not itself trace a mechanistic route into the carcinogenic cascade, so the intermediates are unknown rather than known.

Excess salt worsens the gastritis and atrophy stages that Correa links to salt intake alongside the infection itself. The intervening steps are not nodes in this graph. Recorded as exacerbating rather than triggering, in contrast to the infection link into this same node, because salt worsens a gastritis it does not by itself cause.

Salt exposure continues to act after the initiating gastritis, worsening the atrophy, metaplasia and dysplasia stages that make up this preinvasive substrate. Mucosal injury and intragastric nitrosation are the known intervening steps, and neither is a node in this graph.

nodes.description: Peritoneal and distant outgrowth is reinforced by angiogenic support and reciprocal signaling with stromal compartments such as omental adipocytes.

evidence.reference_title: Omental adipocytes promote peritoneal metastasis of gastric cancer through the CXCL2-VEGFA axis.
evidence.snippet: Conditioned media derived from OmAd (OmAd-CM) promoted the proliferation, migration and capacity to induce angiogenesis of GC cells through AKT phosphorylation and VEGFA overexpression, whereas silencing CXCL2 in OmAd cancelled OmAd-induced effects.

evidence.reference_title: Omental adipocytes promote peritoneal metastasis of gastric cancer through the CXCL2-VEGFA axis.
evidence.snippet: In an orthotopic tumour model using SCID mice, omentectomy suppressed GC growth and peritoneal dissemination, and reduced serum levels of CXCL2.

evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive molecular characterization of gastric adenocarcinoma.
evidence.snippet: CDH1 somatic mutations were enriched in the genomically stable subtype (37% of cases).

nodes.description: Biallelic inactivation of CDH1 abolishes E-cadherin, the adhesion molecule of the epithelial adherens junction. This is the initiating lesion of the diffuse Lauren route and is the carcinogenic event upstream of the invasion node it feeds.

evidence.reference_title: E-cadherin germline mutations in familial gastric cancer.
evidence.snippet: Sequencing of the E-cadherin gene revealed a G --> T nucleotide substitution in the donor splice consensus sequence of exon 7, leading to a truncated gene product.

nodes.description: Reduced E-cadherin expression weakens epithelial adhesion, promotes infiltrative growth, and facilitates lymphatic, perineural, and peritoneal dissemination, particularly in diffuse-type gastric cancer.

evidence.reference_title: E-Cadherin Immunohistochemical Expression in Gastrointestinal Adenocarcinomas and Its Association With Histological and Prognostic Parameters.
evidence.snippet: Loss of E-cadherin expression in advanced tumor stages, higher nodal metastasis, and perineural invasion elucidate the role of E-cadherin as a useful prognostic immunohistochemical marker in gastrointestinal adenocarcinomas.

nodes.description: Metastatic gastric cancer arises from a primary gastric adenocarcinoma that develops through the multistep Correa cascade of chronic gastritis, atrophy, intestinal metaplasia, and dysplasia. This node collapses the atrophy, intestinal metaplasia and dysplasia stages of that sequence into a single preinvasive substrate; each stage is modeled separately in Gastric_Adenocarcinoma. It precedes the invasive and metastatic biology modeled by the downstream nodes in this entry.

evidence.reference_title: Human gastric carcinogenesis: a multistep and multifactorial process--First American Cancer Society Award Lecture on Cancer Epidemiology and Prevention.
evidence.snippet: Evidence from pathology and epidemiology studies has been provided for a human model of gastric carcinogenesis with the following sequential stages: chronic gastritis; atrophy; intestinal metaplasia; and dysplasia.

nodes.description: Persistent colonisation of the gastric mucosa by Helicobacter pylori establishes a non-resolving active gastritis that the host inflammatory response cannot clear. This is the initiating step of the carcinogenic sequence that produces the primary tumour from which the metastatic disease modeled in this entry arises; the full cascade is curated in Gastric_Adenocarcinoma.

evidence.reference_title: Human gastric carcinogenesis: a multistep and multifactorial process--First American Cancer Society Award Lecture on Cancer Epidemiology and Prevention.
evidence.snippet: The initial stages of gastritis and atrophy have been linked to excessive salt intake and infection with Helicobacter pylori.

evidence.reference_title: Influence of Helicobacter pylori oncoprotein CagA in gastric cancer: A critical-reflective analysis.
evidence.snippet: Helicobacter pylori is a Gram-negative bacterium that inhabits the gastric environment of 60.3% of the world's population and represents the main risk factor for the onset of gastric neoplasms.

evidence.reference_title: [Advances in the application of intragastric flora in the diagnosis and treatment of gastric cancer].
evidence.snippet: Gastric cancer is one of the major causes of cancer-related deaths worldwide, and infection with Helicobacter pylori and EBV, smoking and a salt-heavy diet have been shown to be risk factors for the development of gastric cancer.

evidence.snippet: Gastric cancer is one of the major causes of cancer-related deaths worldwide, and infection with Helicobacter pylori and EBV, smoking and a salt-heavy diet have been shown to be risk factors for the development of gastric cancer.

nodes.description: Gland-forming carcinoma that has breached the basement membrane and invades the lamina propria, submucosa and, in advanced disease, the muscularis propria and serosa. This is the terminal step of the Correa cascade and the primary tumour of the intestinal Lauren route, from which the disseminated disease modeled by the downstream nodes arises.

evidence.reference_title: Human gastric carcinogenesis: a multistep and multifactorial process--First American Cancer Society Award Lecture on Cancer Epidemiology and Prevention.
evidence.snippet: Evidence from pathology and epidemiology studies has been provided for a human model of gastric carcinogenesis with the following sequential stages: chronic gastritis; atrophy; intestinal metaplasia; and dysplasia.

evidence.reference_title: Amplification of HER-2 in gastric carcinoma: association with Topoisomerase IIalpha gene amplification, intestinal type, poor prognosis and sensitivity to trastuzumab.
evidence.snippet: HER-2/neu amplification is common in the intestinal type of gastric carcinoma, and it is associated with a poor outcome.

nodes.description: Peritoneal spread in gastric cancer is reinforced by interactions between tumor cells and peritoneal mesothelial cells, helping establish invasive implants, serosal disease, and malignant ascites.

evidence.reference_title: Tks5 activation in mesothelial cells creates invasion front of peritoneal carcinomatosis.
evidence.snippet: The peritoneal dissemination of gastric cancer was significantly increased by mixing cancer cells and PMCs, and was suppressed by knockdown of Tks5 in PMCs.

evidence.reference_title: Smoking and gastric cancer: systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies.
evidence.snippet: Our study provides solid evidence to classify smoking as the most important behavioral risk factor for gastric cancer.
